title: How many CPE hours do CPAs need, and what do the NASBA and AICPA standards require?
description: US CPA CPE explained: the AICPA and NASBA CPE Standards revised for 2026, and CPE hours and ethics rules in New York, California, Texas and Florida.
shortAnswer: Continuing professional education (CPE) hours for US certified public accountants are set by each state board of accountancy, while the Statement on Standards for CPE Programs, published jointly by the AICPA and NASBA, governs how programs are designed and measured. As at November 2026, Texas requires 120 hours every three years, California and Florida 80 hours every two years, and New York 40 hours each calendar year, and each state adds its own ethics requirement.
keyTakeaways: The Statement on Standards for CPE Programs defines one CPE credit as 50 minutes of participation, and boards of accountancy have final authority on acceptance of individual courses.
Revised 2026 Standards took effect August 1, 2026 for new delivery method applications, March 1, 2027 for new programs and November 1, 2028 for programs existing on July 31, 2026.
Texas: 120 credits per three years with 20 a year, plus a board-approved 4 credit ethics course every two years (22 TAC 523.112 and 523.130).

California: 80 hours per two years with 20 a year, 4 hours ethics, and a 2 hour Regulatory Review course every six years. Florida: 80 hours per two years with 8 accounting and auditing and 4 board-approved ethics.
New York: 40 contact hours a year in recognized areas, or 24 concentrated in one recognized area, plus 4 ethics hours every three years (8 NYCRR 70.9).
jurisdiction: United States (national program standards; New York, California, Texas and Florida licensing rules)
regulator: State boards of accountancy (New York State Education Department, California Board of Accountancy, Texas State Board of Public Accountancy, Florida Board of Accountancy), with program standards from the AICPA and NASBA
appliesTo: Licensed CPAs renewing active licenses in each state
CPAs who perform attest, audit or preparation engagements, who face extra subject requirements in some states
CPE sponsors and in-house training teams in accounting firms that issue CPE credit
Out of state licensees who rely on their principal place of business state

sections.heading: Who sets CPE requirements for US CPAs?

blocks.text: Two layers apply. State boards of accountancy set how many hours a licensee must complete and in which subjects; the Statement on Standards for Continuing Professional Education (CPE) Programs sets how programs must be built, measured and documented.

The [NASBA Registry standards page](https://www.nasbaregistry.org/the-standards) explains that the Statement is published jointly by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) and the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy (NASBA). The 2026 Statement itself says CPAs "are responsible for complying with all applicable CPE requirements, rules, and regulations of boards of accountancy", and that boards of accountancy, membership associations and other professional organizations "have final authority on the acceptance of individual courses for CPE credit."

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the 2026 Statement on Standards for CPE Programs and state rules read as at November 2026. State rules change frequently; licensees in other states should check their own board.

sections.heading: What do the AICPA and NASBA CPE Standards require?

blocks.text: The Standards define what counts as a credit and what a program must contain. Under the 2026 Statement, "Fifty minutes of participation in a formal learning program equals one CPE credit." Sponsored learning activities must be based on relevant learning objectives and outcomes, and the Statement sets requirements for program quality, participant engagement, completion verification, measurement, participant communication and documentation.

items: **Delivery methods.** Programs are classified as group programs, self study programs (including nano learning, which focuses on a single learning objective) or blended learning programs.
**Increments.** Group programs can award an initial half or full credit, then one-fifth or one-half increments after the first full credit, although state boards may differ on acceptable increments.
**Self study reinforcement.** Self study programs use review questions or other content reinforcement tools with feedback; a program marketed for 0.2 credit does not need a scored review question.
**Fields of study.** NASBA's Fields of Study document, revised in 2024, classifies credits into subject areas and is referenced by the Standards.

blocks.text: The Standards were revised in 2026. NASBA approved the revisions in April and the AICPA in May 2026. Unless a state sets otherwise, the changes apply from August 1, 2026 for initial or additional delivery method applications, from March 1, 2027 for programs in development or published for the first time, and by November 1, 2028 for group or self study programs that already existed on July 31, 2026. Firms that build their own CPE should plan course updates against those dates, using a method like [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How do CPE hours and ethics requirements compare across states?

blocks.text: The four boards examined use different cycles and ethics rules, so a CPA licensed in several states cannot rely on one calendar. The table summarizes the general renewal requirement for active licensees.

sections.heading: What do Texas and California require in detail?

blocks.text: **Texas.** Under [22 Texas Administrative Code section 523.112](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/22-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-523-112), "A licensee shall complete at least 120 CPE credits in each three-year period, and a minimum of 20 CPE credits in each one-year period." New licensees phase in, reporting 20 credits for the second license year, 60 for the third and 100 for the fourth before the full 120 applies. Section 523.130 requires a board-approved four credit ethics course on the Board's Rules of Professional Conduct every two years, reported on the annual renewal at least every second year.

**California.** The [California Board of Accountancy CE quick reference](https://www.dca.ca.gov/cba/licensees/cequickref.shtml) requires 80 hours of CE in the two years before license expiration, with at least 20 hours in each year including 12 technical hours, 4 hours of ethics, and a 2 hour Board-approved Regulatory Review course if more than six years have passed since the last one.

The ethics and Regulatory Review courses are not interchangeable. At least 40 hours must be technical, licensees doing accounting and auditing or government auditing need 24 hours in that subject plus 4 hours of fraud CE, and hours cannot be carried over. From January 2026 licensees certify completion at renewal instead of listing courses, and the CBA advises keeping CE records for four years for its expanded compliance program.

sections.heading: What do Florida and New York require in detail?

blocks.text: **Florida.** Florida Administrative Code [rule 61H1-33.003](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/florida/Fla-Admin-Code-Ann-R-61H1-33-003) requires each active Florida CPA to complete, during the two-year period, "at least 80 hours of educational instruction or training in public accounting subjects", of which at least 8 hours must be accounting or auditing related, no more than 20 may be behavioral subjects, and at least 4 must be Florida Board-approved ethics. Completion is reported in the DBPR online portal by July 31 before biennial renewal.

**New York.** Under [8 NYCRR 70.9](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/8-NYCRR-70.9), licensees choose each calendar year between at least 40 contact hours in recognized areas (accounting, attest, auditing, taxation, advisory services and specialized knowledge, among others) or at least 24 contact hours concentrated in any one of those recognized areas. Licensees who supervise attest or compilation services, or sign financial statement reports for a firm, need at least 40 contact hours in audit, accounting or attest in the three years before performing that work. Registered licensees must also complete at least 4 contact hours of professional ethics during each three calendar year period, which can count toward the annual hours.

sections.heading: What evidence should firms keep for CPA CPE?

blocks.text: Firms should hold sponsor certificates that show credits, field of study and delivery method, mapped to each licensee's state cycle. That lets the same record answer a board audit, a peer review question or an AICPA membership check. The general method is in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

blocks.text: Firms that also employ Australian or Portuguese accountants can compare these rules with [CPA Australia CPD requirements](/regulations/cpa-australia-cpd-requirements) and the [Portugal OCC continuing training rules](/regulations/portugal-ordem-dos-contabilistas-certificados-cpd). Tax preparers working with lawyers on multi-state matters may find the [attorney CLE comparison](/regulations/us-attorney-cle-requirements-by-state) useful for joint training plans.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry captures learning objectives, field of study and the engagement mechanism for each internal program at design time, which are the elements the CPE Standards ask sponsors to document. Completions are held against each CPA's state cycles, so a firm in the [professional services sector](/industries/professional-services) can show both program design and individual compliance.

faqs.q: How long is one CPE credit?
faqs.a: Under the AICPA and NASBA Statement on Standards for CPE Programs, fifty minutes of participation in a formal learning program equals one CPE credit. After the first full credit, credits may be awarded in one-fifth or one-half increments, although individual state boards may differ.

faqs.q: Does every state require an ethics course for CPAs?
faqs.a: The four states examined all do, but on different schedules: Texas requires a board-approved 4 credit course every two years, California 4 hours each renewal, Florida 4 hours of board-approved ethics each two-year period, and New York 4 hours in each three calendar year period.

faqs.q: Can California CPAs carry over extra CE hours?
faqs.a: No. The California Board of Accountancy says all CE must be completed during the two-year license period and hours cannot be carried from one renewal period to another, even if a licensee renews early and completes more CE before expiration.

faqs.q: When do the 2026 CPE Standards apply to existing courses?
faqs.a: Unless a state board sets otherwise, group and self study programs that already existed on July 31, 2026 must reflect the changes by November 1, 2028. New programs follow from March 1, 2027, and new delivery method applications from August 1, 2026.
